title: A foam link's hover popup shows the issue rendered as markdown
body:
Hovering a `foam:` link runs the hover command from `[links.schemes.foam]` in `config.toml`, which is `foam show {target} --plain`. `popup` in `links.rs` passes the output through `clean` and shows at most `POPUP_LINES` (15) of its lines as plain text. An issue body is markdown, so the popup shows its `##` headings, backticks, fences and tables as typed characters.

coax renders agent messages with `cmr`, through `cmr::parse` and `cmr::layout_marked` in `ui.rs`. The popup could lay out an issue the same way.

## Open

- Where coax gets the markdown. `foam show --plain` prints the issue's header lines, body and notes as one text. `foam show --json` gives the fields apart, so coax could render the body and notes with `cmr` and draw the header itself. Reading JSON ties the popup to foam's output. Today any scheme's hover output is opaque text.
- Whether rendering applies to foam alone or to any scheme, through a setting on the scheme.
- How the 15-line cap counts rendered lines, and whether the popup scrolls.
close_reason: Landed in 365fd6a. hover_command runs foam show --json for a foam link, markdown_popup in links.rs turns the issue into markdown, and markdown_popup_rows in ui.rs lays it out with cmr. An output that is not an issue's JSON falls back to plain lines.
